rationale: Use a broad scouting gradient with a strong final solvent to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while limiting late-elution risk. The midpoint temperature leaves room to improve selectivity in either direction.
The first method already achieves the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to reduce analysis time while testing whether the ample resolution margins are preserved.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to seek earlier elution while retaining the strongest endpoint. Check the early pair for loss of retention, since it is already close to the gradient arrival window.
Raise temperature one step to accelerate the last peak while exploiting the improved minimum resolution of 1.77. Keep the solvent program fixed to measure whether this margin tolerates heating.

Increase the starting organic fraction one step to seek a shorter elution window at the current temperature. This tests whether a narrower gradient span still helps the critical pair or whether weak initial retention now compresses it.
